messages:
maria_support: Customer 'acme-ingest' reporting a burst of 429s during a short window. They saw failures between 2029-03-25T09:12:00Z and 2029-03-25T09:18:30Z. They provided a few X-Request-Id values and a short timeline. cc @sam_se @jordan_infra

sam_se: Thanks — can you ask them for a minimal curl that reproduces the 429s and the full response headers (X-RateLimit-*, x-request-id, x-forwarded-for)? Also need their account_id and org_id for lookup.

maria_support: Pasting the partial headers they already gave. I'll ask them for a HAR and a --trace output.

--- customer-provided headers ---
x-request-id: 01F4A3BCD2
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 14
status: 429
content-type: application/json
--- end ---

jordan_infra: I'll start by scanning ingress and quota metrics for that window. Can you get a representative curl? Example to ask them to run (redact the key when posting here):

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Client-ID: acme-ingest' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: <client-generated-id>' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/mega","prompt":"status check"}'

ops-bot: [automated] RateLimitAlert: spike detected 2029-03-25T09:12:34Z -> 2029-03-25T09:18:59Z; 429 count: 342; top client: acme-ingest; affected nodes: rtf-3, rtf-4

sam_se: Also request they run: curl --dump-header headers.txt --trace-ascii trace.txt ... that gives us request/response bytes and TLS negotiation details. Ask them to include x-request-id values from the trace.

acme_engineer: Hey team — I ran a quick repro locally (12 parallel workers) and hit 429 on iteration 14. Here's the minimal repro we used and the exact response: 

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Client-ID: acme-ingest' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: 01F4A3BCD2' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/mega","prompt":"ping"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 25 Mar 2029 09:12:46 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 14
X-Request-Id: 01F4A3BCD2

{"error":{"message":"Quota exceeded: per-minute burst limit","type":"rate_limit"}}

acme_engineer: I'll attach the --trace output and a HAR after our maintenance slot in ~30m.

maria_support: Putting this into ticket #INC-123456. @jordan_infra can you check if this aligns with our smoothing/bursting behavior? If it's hitting a single quota window we can advise a temporary burst raise or recommend client-side backoff.

jordan_infra: Quick look at ingress: their traffic pattern shows a tight burst with 12 parallel connections from same client aggregate. Tokens/sec peaked and triggered distributed token throttling across rtf-3 and rtf-4. Uploading a 5-min log snapshot to the ticket and mapping the request ids to backend traces now.

--- logs snippet (ingress sampling) ---
2029-03-25T09:12:40Z rtf-3 incoming request X-Request-Id=01F4A3BCD0 client=acme-ingest tokens=512
2029-03-25T09:12:41Z rtf-4 incoming request X-Request-Id=01F4A3BCD1 client=acme-ingest tokens=512
2029-03-25T09:12:46Z rtf-3 response 429 X-Request-Id=01F4A3BCD2
2029-03-25T09:12:49Z rtf-4 response 429 X-Request-Id=01F4A3BCD3
--- end ---

sam_se: Action items for support: 1) get HAR + --trace bundle, 2) full curl output (headers + body), 3) account_id/org_id, 4) confirm parallel worker count and whether they use retries. I'll draft an explanation for client-side backoff and token pacing. :thumbsup:

acme_engineer: Confirmed — we run 12 workers, no client-side pacing currently. We'll send the bundles within 30 mins. Thanks for the quick triage.

maria_support: Thanks — keeping this open until we get the HAR. Will update the ticket when logs mapping is done. :white_check_mark:
